question: Is the provider-fidelity evidence sufficient to accept these Matrix, Mattermost, Signal, Slack, recorder, and HTTP contract changes, or must the branch add authoritative source and actual-client proof before merge?
rationale: The repository policy requires provider-native fidelity and discourages treating OpenClaw-only tests as sufficient, while this branch changes several externally observable contracts and compatibility boundaries at once.

options.title: Require targeted fidelity proof
options.body: Remove the changelog entry and add a concise contract matrix with authoritative citations plus redacted exact-head client or Crabbox output for representative success, retry, rejection, and committed-delivery paths.

options.title: Accept test-backed contracts
options.body: Approve the documented compatibility changes based on the focused regression suite and accept the remaining risk without additional live-client evidence.

options.title: Split by provider
options.body: Separate the shared recorder/HTTP work and individual provider changes so each contract can receive narrower evidence and review.

recommendation.title: Require targeted fidelity proof
recommendation.body: Remove the changelog entry and add a concise contract matrix with authoritative citations plus redacted exact-head client or Crabbox output for representative success, retry, rejection, and committed-delivery paths.

likelyOwner.reason: This repository member is the strongest available security and protocol-domain routing candidate for the cross-provider contract decision.
